name: Karpathy-Inspired Claude Code Guidelines
works_with: Claude Code (as a plugin or a CLAUDE.md file) and Cursor (as a project rule)
short: One CLAUDE.md file with four rules that push your coding agent to ask first, write less code and make smaller diffs.
what: A single instruction file built from Andrej Karpathy's notes on where LLMs go wrong when coding. It sets four principles: think before coding, keep it simple, change only what the task needs, and work toward goals you can verify with tests. You install it as a plugin or drop it into your project's CLAUDE.md.
who: Anyone whose coding agent makes assumptions without asking, overbuilds, or edits code it wasn't asked to touch. The README says the rules favour caution over speed, so for typo fixes and one-liners you may find it slows things down.
needs: Claude Code for the plugin route, or any project where you keep a CLAUDE.md

try.label: From the README
try.text: Give it a task like "Fix the bug" and see whether it writes a test that reproduces the bug first. The README says it's working when clarifying questions come before the code and your diffs only hold the changes you asked for.

watch: The install commands fetch from `forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills`, a different GitHub path from the one in the newsletter. That's what the README says to use.
The file route downloads text straight into your CLAUDE.md. Read what it adds before you commit it.
The rules favour caution over speed, and the README says to use judgement on trivial tasks.
